page: Microsoft Azure E64ns_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor supplying 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory totals 512.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-bound applications. The processor includes a large 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix acceleration. The instance does not include local ephemeral storage and requires remote network-attached disks for persistent storage operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory subsystems and compute processing capabilities. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 378.82 GB/sec, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances, alongside 144.8 GB/sec in write throughput. In compute evaluations, the PassMark CPU score reaches 70602.13, supported by strong cryptographic and extended instruction capabilities. In memory-dependent application testing, the instance delivered 76.16 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and recorded 30184.35 in PassMark database operations. In addition, hardware-accelerated matrix instructions deliver strong LLM prompt processing throughput across small, medium, and large model architectures.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E64ns_v6 maximizes resource density for memory-heavy computing without requiring specialized accelerator silicon. The inclusion of AMX hardware units allows users to run moderate machine learning inference workloads without provisioning dedicated GPUs. A notable operational tradeoff is the complete absence of bundled local storage, meaning input/output throughput is tied directly to network-attached storage tiers and associated remote disk costs.

The Azure E64ns_v6 is best suited for large in-memory databases such as Redis or Apache Ignite, relational database management systems, real-time analytics engines, enterprise business applications, and CPU-based vector search or transformer inference.
